pages.lesson:
LESSON: LISTENING FOR INFORMATION, ORAL EXPRESSION

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: GERMAN
Strand: Listening and speaking
Topic 1.6: Listening for information, Oral Expression

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Listening for information, Oral Expression
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: Why is it important to use polite language?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. identify specific information from given texts
2. use acquired grammar structures for oral expression and communication
3. appreciate the role of appropriate oral expression in everyday communication

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Listening for information, Oral Expression

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Listening for information, Oral Expression

Teach
• Focus skill: identify specific information from given texts.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Listening for information, Oral Expression.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Listening for information, Oral Expression
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is it important to use polite language?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
